title: Voronoi-Markov chain and spatial entropy for point pattern analysis
claim: Proposed spatial entropy and Markov-chain metrics respond systematically to increasing point clustering, with behavior varying by sample size.
layout: Left 2x3 point-pattern grid; right 2x4 metric-curve grid; shared x-axis
description: The figure has two parts. Panel (a), on the left, is a 2x3 grid of unit discs filled with Voronoi tessellations of random points. Rows are concentration q=1 and q=0, and columns are N=32, 128 and 512 points. Each disc is labeled with its dense basin entropy H_db. Cells are drawn in pale orange. Points crowd toward the center when q is higher. Panel (b), on the right, is a 2x4 grid of line plots against concentration q. The columns show dense basin entropy, Voronoi-Markov entropy rate, spectral gap, and Delaunay angle Cramér-von Mises p-values. The top row shows raw metrics and the bottom row shows normalized or scaled variants. Each plot has several curves for log2 N from 4 to 9, with shaded bands. Curves use a color gradient per metric: purple, red, brown/orange, and blue/cyan. Most curves decline as q rises. The eye goes first to the colorful curve grid.
caption: The concentrated disc model for various degrees of concentration $q$, evaluated with the dense basin entropy, metrics derived from the Voronoi-Markov chain, and Delaunay triangulation angle statistics.
abstract: In this paper, we revisit the concept of entropy in the spatial context with the aim of deriving computable and interpretable metrics for point pattern analysis in domains such as histopathology. We discuss stochastic point process assumptions like Poisson homogeneity and Simple Sequential Inhibition (SSI) and review established results for Voronoi and Delaunay tilings of point sets for their potential to provide null distributions for rigorous empirical hypothesis testing. We present (1) a novel "dense basin entropy" defined in terms of the Ord distribution supported on Voronoi basins, which is shown to be sensitive to clustering, and (2) a related Markov chain designed as a simplification or approximation of Brownian motion in the underlying planar domain. We investigate bounds on the dense basin entropy in the SSI regime and in empirical data, and show that the entropy rate and spectral gap of the Markov chain lead to sharp discrimination metrics. Finally, we demonstrate a generalization to multiple-set analysis via aggregation of one set over the Markov invariant measure for another. Simulations and experiments in histopathology show that our proposed metrics offer insights complementary to other instantiations of entropy in spatial analysis. The code can be found on our SMProfiler GitHub: https://github.com/nadeemlab/SMProfiler.
